Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Billing Sales is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who both lead and advise on deals for one of the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio. Billing Sales is tasked with attacking a $100B market opportunity for automating the entire order to cash process.

What you’ll do

As the Manager, Billing Sales (Enterprise) at Stripe, you will use your leadership and management skills to manage and grow a team of Account Executives to help drive growth of Stripe Billing for sellers in the Americas. You will collaborate with the core sales leadership, marketing, product marketing, and product teams to develop deep product and industry knowledge and drive strategic deals. You will own the coaching, development, and performance of your team, driving the forecast of the region. You will be instrumental in leading in-depth product discussions with existing and prospective customers – and building and executing against our go-to-market strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Recruit, develop and lead a team of product sales executives focused on the SaaS business within the AMER region.
  • Create go-to-market plans and solutions to meet our customer needs, in collaboration with Product, Sales, Finance and Marketing stakeholders.
  • Manage day-to-day operations, with a focus on performance against key sales metrics.
  • Be accountable for driving revenue, increasing attach rates, and new client acquisition at high rates of growth.
  • Coach and guide the team in developing consultative and solution-based sales skills through all facets of the sales cycle.
  • Get hands on engaged in the largest, most strategic opportunities, leading executive relationships and helping the team win new customers.
  • Inspire, motivate, and enable individual development to promote career growth of direct reports.
  • Lead with clarity and context with a compelling plan in line with Stripe’s direction.
  • Create structure and focus for GTM ideas and product sales campaigns that the product team is exploring. Drive execution and measurement. Analyze results and make recommendations for action in a timely manner.
  • Constantly innovate and improve programs and program management mechanisms, suggesting new ideas, sharing best practices, and improving the business and customer engagement model.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of technology sales experience with 5+ years of people leadership experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in payments, billing, tax, or relevant SaaS industry.
  • Experience leading sales, new business and operations in an early stage, high-growth technology environment
  • Ability to hire, train and coach a high-performance sales team
  • Ability to build relationships with strategic client and industry thought leaders
  • Demonstrated passion for Stripe’s mission

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience in Billing, Finance, Tax, or other relevant SaaS product field
  • Prior experience at a growth stage Internet/software company
  • Prior experience in enterprise sales, partnerships and/or business development
descriptions.job-0t724ra:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
 
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
 
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions.
 
Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out.
 
You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries.
  • Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline.
  • Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release.
  • Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision.
  • Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers.
  • Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product.
  • Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team.
  • Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads.
  • Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You  

  • 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team.
  • Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required.
  • Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output.
  • Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting.
  • Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus.
  • Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle.
  • Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee.
  • Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting.
  • Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale.
  • Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.
  • Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit.
  • A CPA, chartered tax adviser, or equivalent; or a degree in data science, computer science, or accounting.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package
  • L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
  • Various team building programs and company events
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

Phantom is on a mission to connect the world to the freedom of open markets. Tens of millions of people all over the world use Phantom to access global markets that never close, including perpetuals, prediction markets, tokenized assets, stablecoins and memes. Phantom users are able to discover the markets that matter and the cultural moments that shape them, building conviction through real-time data and the verified performance of top traders. With self-custody and access to open networks at its core, Phantom lets them control their financial moves in the same app they use to safely store or spend money worldwide.

Phantom has reached #1 in Google Play's finance category and consistently ranks in the top 50 apps across all categories. Check out our Forbes Fintech 50 and CNBC and Statista's World's Top Fintech Companies 2026!

We are around 180 people, fully remote, backed by a $150M Series C investment from a16z, Sequoia Capital and Paradigm.

Responsibilities

As a Data Scientist at Phantom, you’ll help shape our consumer products through rigorous analysis, experimentation, and reliable data. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, and Growth to understand user behavior, identify opportunities, and guide product decisions.

  • Analyze user journeys, activation, engagement, retention, and monetization to identify opportunities and recommend product improvements.

  • Design and evaluate A/B tests, including hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, sample sizing, and interpretation. Communicate uncertainty and distinguish observed relationships from causal effects.

  • Define and maintain product metrics, and partner with Engineering to improve instrumentation and validate the data behind them.

  • Build reusable analytical datasets and dbt models using SQL. Collaborate with Data Engineering on Snowflake, Dagster, and ETL pipelines to improve data quality and support analysis.

  • Use Python for statistical analysis, modeling, and automation. Make your work reproducible, documented, and maintainable.

  • Incorporate AI coding tools such as Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor into your workflow to accelerate development and analysis. Review and validate generated code, assumptions, and results.

  • Independently lead ambiguous problems from initial question through analysis, recommendation, and measurement. Communicate clearly, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence priorities across teams.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, or a related field, with a demonstrated record of influencing product decisions.

  • Strong foundation in statistics, including probability, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, regression, and sources of bias and confounding. Ability to select appropriate methods and explain their assumptions and limitations.

  • Practical experience designing and analyzing A/B tests, including defining metrics, assessing statistical power, checking experiment validity, and translating results into decisions.

  • Advanced SQL skills and strong proficiency in Python for data exploration, statistical analysis, and reproducible analytical workflows.

  • Working knowledge of dbt, data modeling, and modern data platforms. Familiarity with orchestration tools such as Dagster and how ETL pipelines, dependencies, and refresh schedules affect downstream analysis.

  • Hands-on experience using AI coding tools such as Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor in your regular workflow, with the judgment to verify correctness and maintain code quality.

  • Experience partnering directly with product teams, ideally on consumer products, to understand behavior and improve activation, engagement, retention, or monetization.

  • Ability to independently structure ambiguous problems, prioritize work, and communicate recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners.

  • Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn unfamiliar systems and follow through on useful work.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with Snowflake, including querying large datasets and understanding query performance and cost.

  • Experience with crypto, tokenized assets, finance, or fintech.

Why Work With Us

Phantom's journey to becoming a global trading app began with making crypto easier to use. Today, we’re building on that foundation to help people discover the markets that matter, make informed financial moves, and safely store or spend their money worldwide. Joining Phantom means helping shape that next chapter: building products that bring the freedom of open markets to more people.

 

  • Build for global impact: Create products used by tens of millions of people, making innovative financial markets more accessible to users around the world.

  • Make complexity feel simple: Solve meaningful challenges across design, engineering, and user experience to make discovering markets and managing money seamless.

  • Put users in control: Help build a future where people have greater freedom over their assets and financial decisions, with security and self-custody at the foundation.

Benefits (only available to full-time employees)

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Comprehensive insurance (medical/dental/vision): base plan 100% covered

  • Flexible hours and a long-standing, supportive remote environment

  • Unlimited vacation: Take time when you need it (and we really mean it!)

  • 401(k) retirement plan

  • Wellness stipend

  • Weekly meal stipend

  • Learning & Development stipend

  • Remote / WFH set-up stipend

We strongly encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We believe that our work is stronger with a variety of perspectives, and we’re eager to further diversify our company. If you have a background that you feel would make an impact at Phantom, please consider applying. We’re committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best work of your career.

By submitting your resume and application materials, you acknowledge and agree that Phantom Technologies, Inc. ("Phantom") collects and processes your personal information (including application materials, interview records, and related data) to evaluate your candidacy. Phantom may use AI-powered tools and third-party service providers for transcription, note-taking, scheduling, and other administrative tasks. Phantom does not sell your information and your materials will be handled securely and in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

Whether you're new to crypto or an experienced user, Trust Wallet makes it easier, safer, and more convenient to explore Web3, securely access dApps, manage your crypto, and buy and sell digital assets, all in one place.


Build what’s next in Web3. Grow into a leader.

About the Programme

The Trust Wallet Graduate Leadership Programme is a selective, 12-month fast track for ambitious early-career talent who want to shape the future of Web3 and grow into its next generation of leaders.

At Trust Wallet, you won’t spend your first year watching from the sidelines. You’ll take ownership of meaningful projects from day one, work on products used by millions globally, and collaborate with exceptional talent across a fast-moving, global Web3 business.

Starting in one of our core functional teams, you’ll build deep expertise, gain cross-functional experience, and turn bold ideas into solutions that create real value for users and the business. With mentorship from senior leaders and opportunities to take on increasing responsibility, you’ll develop the judgement, commercial mindset and execution skills to make an impact.

How the Programme Works

  • Think beyond your role: Work across functions, learn from experienced leaders, and turn insights into ideas that improve the user experience, unlock business opportunities or create new ways of working. The strongest ideas can progress into real initiatives, products or launches.

  • Growth & Ecosystem: Contribute to go-to-market strategies, growth experiments, community initiatives and partnerships across wallets, dApps, blockchains, stablecoins and emerging payment networks.

  • Clear communication: You can articulate complex ideas simply, influence through sound reasoning and collaborate effectively across different teams.

  • AI-native and future-focused: You actively explore AI tools such as Claude, Grok and Cursor, and are curious about AI agents and how they could transform how people work and transact.

  • Genuine Web3 curiosity: You’ve explored wallets, DEXs, stablecoins or other Web3 applications, and have ideas about what works, what doesn’t and what could be better.

  • Adaptable and driven: You learn quickly, thrive in ambiguity and are motivated by high standards, rapid execution and meaningful challenges.

Nice to Have

  • Entrepreneurial experience: You’ve founded a venture, built a product or launched a project in AI or crypto — whether or not it succeeded.

  • Hands-on Web3 involvement: Experience with DeFi, perpetuals, stablecoin payments, hackathons, DAOs or other ecosystem initiatives.

  • A track record of building: Side projects, product teardowns, research, a newsletter, open-source contributions or an active presence on X or GitHub.

What You’ll Get

  • A launchpad for leadership: A structured 12-month development journey with mentorship from senior leaders and opportunities to grow your scope and responsibility.

  • Ownership that matters: The chance to work on real challenges and deliver improvements for a global user base of millions.

  • A front-row seat to the future: Hands-on exposure to self-custody, AI-powered experiences, crypto payments and the evolving Web3 ecosystem.

  • A steep learning curve: Learn by doing, collaborate across functions and build commercial, strategic and execution capabilities early in your career.

  • A pathway to grow: High performers can progress into permanent roles where their strengths and ambitions align with Trust Wallet’s evolving needs.

Think boldly. Build with purpose. Help shape the future of Web3.

Additional Information

This is a global and fully remote role. You must have the right to work for the country you are based.

Why work at Trust Wallet?

  • Be a part of the world’s leading blockchain ecosystem that continues to grow.

  • Excellent learning and career development opportunities.

Our platform’s unrivalled uptime, scalability, depth and breadth of our data and intelligence means exacting organizations choose Elliptic for their compliance, risk management, intelligence operations and blockchain infrastructure needs.

Founded in 2013, Elliptic is headquartered in London with offices in New York, Washington D.C., UAE, Singapore and Tokyo. To learn more, visit www.elliptic.co and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

 

Do you want to lead a data science team on a problem the industry has not solved yet, while still writing code yourself? Are you excited about building the data foundation for how compliance works when the customer is an autonomous agent rather than a person? Are you looking for a values led company where a small team is trusted with a question that matters commercially in months, not years?

 

The impact you will have:

You will lead data science inside Elliptic's Intelligence team, alongside Intelligence Collection, Research and Investigations, and Professional Services. This is deliberately a player-coach role with a prospect of scaling a team. At first you will lead a small team of data scientists and you are expected to own the team's direction, performance and growth. You will own the evidence for the models your team builds, and you will represent them at Elliptic's model risk governance forum. This is not a compliance tax bolted onto the technical work: it is the reason institutions trust our outputs.

The reason we are hiring a lead as we add more data scientists is that a small team working on an unsolved problem needs someone who intrinsically understands the domain, not a layer of management above it. You will set what this team works on, hire the next people into it, and be the person whose technical judgement the team trusts because you can do the work yourself.

 

What you will do:

  • Lead and grow the team. Set objectives with your data scientists in the context of company strategy, own their performance and development, and be the manager who has the difficult conversation rather than deferring it. Level the team against Elliptic's Intelligence career framework and build real development paths.

  • Hire the next data scientists. Own the hiring process end to end with support: levels, job descriptions, hiring plan, interview panel and bar, and the hiring decision. Team growth to seven to nine people over time depends on you getting this right early.

  • Build the collection for the future of compliance. Take it from a directive to a specification to delivered data: define what good looks like, sequence the work, set the quality bar, and be honest about what the dataset does and does not support.

  • Own model governance for your team's models. Keep the model inventory current and correctly tiered, make sure validation and testing evidence exists at the standard each tier requires, monitor for drift and act on threshold breaches, and submit material changes and production deployments for review with the testing artefacts attached. Own the remediation of issues raised against your models, to agreed deadlines.

  • Lead Elliptic's data science work. Frame the research question, run the first experiments, and form a defensible view of what Elliptic needs to be able to do and by when. Bring that view to Intelligence leadership, the Chief Scientist and Product as a recommendation rather than as an open question.

  • Stay technically hands on. Write code, review your team's work at the level of method rather than output, and make the method calls yourself when they matter.

  • Own the team's existing commitments. The team's current work on clustering, attribution, heuristics and labelling continues to serve the platform. You own its reliability and its trade offs, and you decide what to stop.

  • Work across functions. Partner with Intelligence Collection, Collection Engineering, Research and Investigations, the Chief Scientist, Product and Engineering, so that data science work lands as platform capability rather than as analysis nobody uses.

  • Set the AI working standard for the team. Decide how your team uses AI in its engineering and research workflow, what must be verified and how, and hold the team to it.

 

What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

  • The collection plan delivered at a scale that supports real model or heuristic work, with a documented path to maintaining it.

  • An agreed Elliptic position on the evolution of compliance systems, timed against expected industry demand, with the first capability work either underway or deliberately deferred with stated reasons.

  • At least one data science hire made, and the existing levelled against the career framework with development plans in place.

  • Model governance in good standing for everything your team owns: inventory current and correctly tiered, no overdue validations on the highest tiers, monitoring in place with acted-upon thresholds, and no open issues past their remediation deadline.

  • Data science objectives for Intelligence agreed and delivering, with other functions able to state what they can expect from the team and when.

  • A visible improvement in the reliability or throughput of the team's core output, attributable to a change you made.

  • Technical credibility intact: the team takes your method judgements seriously because you can do the work.

 

You will be a great fit here if you:

  • Want to lead a team without leaving the technical work behind, and can say honestly where you draw that line.

  • Are comfortable being accountable for a question nobody has answered yet, including for saying what you do not know.

  • Treat management as the work rather than as overhead: objectives, feedback, development and difficult conversations included.

  • Treat governance as part of building good models rather than as paperwork that follows them, and would rather surface a problem with your own model than have someone else find it.

  • Are pragmatic about trade offs between rigour and speed, and can explain the trade off you chose.

  • Make other teams more effective rather than treating them as consumers of your team's output.

  • Are curious about how the company operates beyond your own function.

  • Care about the mission of using intelligence to fight financial crime and protect the global financial system.

 

Our ideal candidate has:

  • AI fluency, which is essential for this role. You must be able to demonstrate how you apply AI tools and approaches within a data science workflow: writing and debugging code, exploring unfamiliar data, accelerating pipeline and model work, and automating repetitive tasks. You must also be able to show how you critically evaluate the output, where you would not rely on it, and how you set verification expectations for a team rather than only for yourself. This is assessed in a dedicated stage of the interview process, working with your own tooling.

  • Demonstrated experience managing data scientists or machine learning engineers: setting objectives, owning performance including underperformance, and developing people. You can point to someone whose career changed because of how you managed them.

  • Experience hiring into a technical team, including defining the bar rather than only sitting on panels.

  • Deep, hands on data science and machine learning capability that is current. Strong Python and SQL, and the ability to interrogate large behavioural or transactional datasets yourself and defend your method under challenge.

  • A track record of taking an ambiguous question to a delivered dataset, model or capability, including deciding what was good enough.

  • Experience with a modern data stack comparable to ours: a cloud data lake, Spark or Databricks, and AWS.

  • Clear communication with technical and non technical stakeholders, and the ability to cascade direction to a team so that each person knows why their work matters.

 

Bonus Points for:

  • Work on agentic systems, LLM agents or autonomous transaction flows, whether in compliance, payments, fraud or infrastructure.

About Open Standard

Open Standard is building internet-native money. Data moved to the cloud, and dollars will move onchain. When they do, stablecoins become core financial infrastructure.

Our stablecoin, Open USD (OUSD), is built for that shift. Minting and redeeming are free at any volume. Nearly all reserve revenue goes back to the businesses that grow adoption. The partners who use OUSD govern it, rather than a single issuer.

OUSD is live on Base, Ethereum, Solana, and Tempo. Our founding partners are Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa, and more than 200 banks, payment networks, fintechs, and crypto companies have signed up to use OUSD. Our CEO is Zach Abrams, who co-founded Bridge (acquired by Stripe for $1.1B) and previously led product at Brex, Coinbase, and Square.

OS is currently a team of about ten. We have a real shot at being the next inevitable transformation in stablecoins. We're hiring someone to help make us inevitable.

The role

We're hiring a Deputy General Counsel to help build the legal function at Open Standard alongside our General Counsel, a Founding Team member of Open Standard, who was also part of the founding team of Bridge. You'll be a partner to the GC, not a direct report in the usual sense. The two of you will divide the work by comparative advantage, and you'll own your areas end to end. We are AI-centric, highly scaled, and don't plan on building a large legal team for the foreseeable future. You'll do the work yourself, with AI agents and a tight group of outside counsel extending your reach.

Legal sits at the center of OS's business. You'll be integrated into OUSD design choices, partner deals, and launch decisions, all of which present needle moving commercial opportunities that depend on thoughtful legal decision making that unlocks value for the business.

What you'll do

  • Shape the product with our product and engineering teams: mint and redemption flows, partner rewards, wallet and chain integrations, and new use cases from cross-border payments to agentic commerce.

  • Structure and negotiate the deals OUSD runs on: network partner agreements, reserve and custody relationships, exchange and liquidity arrangements, and agreements with chains and protocols.

  • Work directly with the world's largest banks, card networks, and asset managers, answering their diligence, risk, and regulatory questions with credibility.

  • Find the creative structure when the easy answer is "no": the deal term, product change, or regulatory path that gets a partner live.

  • Help steward a new kind of governance model, with a company owned and governed by the partners who use its product.

  • Support our Head of Policy on regulator and policymaker engagement, comment letters, and industry work.

  • Assist with regulatory strategy for OUSD under the GENIUS Act and state and international regimes. This covers licensing paths, issuer and reserve arrangements, and how rewards and distribution are treated.

  • Build an AI-native legal function, using agents and workflows for contract review, diligence questionnaires, regulatory tracking, and partner questions.

  • Manage outside counsel in the US and abroad tightly, and know when not to use them.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have 10+ years of legal experience, including substantial in-house time at crypto companies.

  • Know the stablecoin market cold from three angles: commercial, regulatory, and product. You can explain how issuers make money, how reserves and redemption work, what GENIUS changes, and where the market is going next.

  • Have worked with or inside large financial institutions and understand how banks, card networks, and asset managers make decisions. You earn their trust without starting to act like them.

  • Have creative commercial instincts and use them to shape deals and products, not just paper them. You're a regulatory and product lawyer who structures deals, not a contracts specialist who knows crypto.

  • Are scrappy and do the work yourself, from the first draft to the board memo.

  • Already use AI seriously in your practice, and have built agents or workflows that expand what one lawyer can do.

  • Write clearly and precisely, because most decisions here start in writing.

  • Are admitted to practice in a US jurisdiction.

Strong candidates may also have

  • Worked in-house at a stablecoin issuer

  • Worked in a bank's digital assets group, alongside crypto-native experience

  • Worked on stablecoin or payments licensing: trust charters, state money transmission, or non-US regimes such as MiCA

  • Helped build the legal function at an early-stage company

  • Relationships with regulators, policymakers, or industry groups in payments and digital assets
